impact_map: 1. Routes: POST /api/v1/agent/tools/{tool_name} and /api/v1/agent/tools/v2/{tool_name} overwrite the body's agent_id with the server principal at backend/app/main.py:1102 and backend/app/main.py:1122, so the adapter's value never reaches the gateway as identity.
2. Principal resolution: backend/app/agent/principal.py:49 states the caller's agent_id is not an input; the actor id comes from backend/app/core/config.py:40 (default citynexus-local-agent).

3. The one predicate that names MCP callers, backend/app/agent/gateway.py:331, is fed that server actor id (backend/app/agent/gateway.py:330), so _agent_id() cannot flip the native PLAN_ONLY boundary; only CITYNEXUS_AGENT_PRINCIPAL_ID can.

4. What _agent_id() does change: measured by driving the real FastMCP object - the wire hint goes from mcp-client to the CITYNEXUS_AGENT_ID value, and on the current line that env var has no effect at all.

5. Existing tests that would go red: none. The HTTP-level witness backend/tests/test_agent_principal_boundary.py already proves the body id is untrusted and the audit actor is the server principal, and it stays 2 passed / 0 failed on the experiment.
6. Product suite: whole collected 1342 with 0 collection errors, harness 72 of 72 passed, exit 0 on the experiment - identical to the landed line.

7. What the user sees on failure: nothing changes. No frontend cell, no status text and no error code reads the adapter hint; the gateway's own agent_id fields (backend/app/agent/gateway.py:528) are built from the overwritten principal.

8. Correction to my own ORD-0334 table row: it said the same file's _agent_id() 'changes principal identity'. Measured against the current line that is wrong - it changes an untrusted hint. The row was written before ORD-0330 and ORD-0336 landed the server-side boundary, so the concern is now closed by evidence, not by argument.

9. runtime_identity.py needs no port at all: the blob is identical on both lines (cb14edcc8747e906503ed8241cc0baa80d1d04e7), so the only remaining blocker for ORD-0337 is the anonymous uncommitted edit in the shared worktree, which is still dirty and is on no ref.

10. Recommendation, not a decision: ORD-0337 is worth at most a validation-lane convenience (naming the principal in locally driven adapter calls, 2 new witnesses). If you want the MCP caller to matter to the product boundary, that is a different order - it would have to change main.py's overwrite or add a scoped credential, which is F's land and yours to sequence.
